1-2.word_for_word: nava-triṃśe — in the thirty-ninth chapter; purīm gacchati acyute — when Acyuta goes to the city; gopikā-uktayaḥ — the words of the gopīs; akrūreṇa kālindyām viṣṇu-lokasya darśanam — Akrūra's vision of Viṣṇu's realm in the Yamunā; bhaktānām manorathāḥ satyā bhavanti — devotees' aspirations become true; rāma-kṛṣṇābhyām uru adhikam mānitaḥ — greatly honored by Rāma and Kṛṣṇa
1-2.translation: In the thirty-ninth chapter are narrated the words of the gopīs when Acyuta departs for the city and Akrūra's vision of Viṣṇu's realm in the Yamunā. The opening shows that the aspirations of devotees come true: Akrūra sat at ease, having been greatly honored by Rāma and Kṛṣṇa.

4.word_for_word: he tāta he saumya — O dear one, O gentle one; svāgatam — welcome; sva-jñāti-bandhūnām — of one's own relatives and connections; suhṛdaḥ — friends; jñātayaḥ sa-piṇḍāḥ — blood relatives sharing the ancestral offering; bandhavaḥ asapiṇḍāḥ sambandhinaḥ — other relations not sharing that lineage; an-amīvam — freedom from evil or suffering; sukham — welfare; anāmayam — health
4.translation: ‘O dear and gentle one, welcome.’ Kṛṣṇa asks about Akrūra's relatives and connections. ‘Jñātis’ are close blood-relatives sharing the ancestral lineage; ‘bandhavas’ are other relations connected to the family. ‘An-amīvam’ means freedom from affliction or suffering—in short, welfare—and ‘anāmayam’ means health.

5.word_for_word: evam praśnaḥ api mama na ati-saṅgataḥ — even this inquiry of mine is not entirely appropriate; aṅga he akrūra — dear Akrūra; pṛcche — I ask; naḥ asmākam kulasya āmaye roge — in the disease afflicting our family; naḥ mātulaḥ iti nāma yasya — the one called our maternal uncle; naḥ svānām jñātīnām — of our own relatives; tasya prajāsu ca — and among his subjects
5.translation: Kṛṣṇa then admits that even such a polite inquiry is scarcely appropriate: ‘Dear Akrūra, I ask, but while the disease of our family—the man called our maternal uncle—remains, what welfare can there be for our relatives or for his subjects?’

6.word_for_word: asmat — because of us; asmat-nimittam — on our account; vṛjinam — suffering; āryayoḥ — of the two venerable ones; niraparādhayoḥ — who are innocent; yad-hetoḥ — because of whom; yaḥ aham eva hetuḥ — I myself am the cause
6.translation: ‘Because of us’ means ‘on our account.’ ‘Vṛjina’ is suffering. The two venerable parents are innocent, and Kṛṣṇa says that he himself is the occasion on account of which that suffering has come upon them.

7.word_for_word: he saumya — O gentle one; svānām vaḥ darśanam — sight of you, our own relation; adya mama sañjātam — has come to me today; tad-diṣṭyā bhadram — by good fortune, this is auspicious
7.translation: ‘O gentle one, today I have at last obtained the sight of you, one of our own people. By good fortune this auspicious meeting has occurred.’

8.word_for_word: mādhavaḥ — Mādhava; madhoḥ vaṃśajaḥ — descendant of Madhu
8.translation: ‘Mādhava’ here means a descendant of Madhu.

9.word_for_word: dhanuḥ-makha-chadmā sandeśaḥ — the message disguised as an invitation to the bow-sacrifice; tad-artham — for that purpose; cāṇūra-ādibhiḥ ghātana-artham — in order to have him killed by Cāṇūra and the others; asya kṛṣṇasya purataḥ varṇayām āsa — he described it before Kṛṣṇa; sva-janma — Kṛṣṇa's own birth; ānakadundubheḥ sakāśāt — as learned from Ānakadundubhi, Vasudeva
9.translation: Akrūra explained before Kṛṣṇa the message whose pretext was the bow-sacrifice, but whose real purpose was to have Kṛṣṇa killed by Cāṇūra and the others. He also related the circumstances of Kṛṣṇa's own birth as he had learned them from Ānakadundubhi, Vasudeva.

10.word_for_word: vijajñatuḥ — they understood distinctly; viśeṣeṇa jñāpayāmāsatuḥ — they made the matter clearly known
10.translation: ‘Vijajñatuḥ’ indicates that the two understood the matter distinctly and fully.

11.word_for_word: nandaḥ gopān samādiśat — Nanda instructed the cowherds; gṛhyatām ity-ādinā — shown by the words beginning ‘let it be collected’; go-rasaḥ — products of the cows; kṣīra-ādiḥ — milk and the like; upāyanāni — presentation gifts; uttama-vastūni — excellent articles
11.translation: Nanda likewise instructed the cowherds, as shown by the command beginning ‘let it be collected.’ ‘Go-rasa’ means products of the cows such as milk, and ‘upāyanas’ are excellent articles to be offered as gifts.

12.word_for_word: rasān — rich preparations; ghṛta-ādīn — ghee and the like; śabda-chalena — by a play on the word rasa; acikitsyasya rogasya cikitsā-artham rasān dāsyāmaḥ — ‘we shall give medicines for the incurable disease’; kṣattrā — by the officer; vraja-rakṣā-adhikṛtena — charged with protecting Vraja; āghoṣayat — proclaimed; sarvataḥ ghoṣitavān — announced everywhere
12.translation: ‘Rasas’ means products such as ghee. By a play on the word, there is also the suggestion: ‘We shall bring rasas as medicine for this incurable disease.’ The kṣattṛ was the official charged with protecting Vraja, and he had the announcement proclaimed everywhere.

13.word_for_word: tāḥ — those women; kṛṣṇa-eka-jīvanāḥ gopyaḥ — the gopīs whose sole life was Kṛṣṇa; tam akrūram āgatam upaśrutya — hearing that Akrūra had arrived
13.translation: The women in question are the gopīs, whose very life was Kṛṣṇa. They heard that Akrūra had arrived.

14.word_for_word: vyathā-liṅgāni āha pañcabhiḥ — five verses describe the signs of their anguish; śravaṇena kṛtaḥ hṛt-tāpaḥ — heart-pain caused by what they heard; tena śvāsaḥ — sighing from that pain; mlānā mukha-śrīḥ — facial beauty faded; dukūlāni valayāni keśa-granthayaḥ ca — fine garments, bracelets and hair-knots; sraṃsantaḥ — slipping loose
14.translation: Five verses describe the outward signs of their anguish. What they heard produced burning pain in their hearts and heavy sighing, so that the beauty of their faces faded. For some, fine garments, bracelets and tied hair all slipped loose.

15.word_for_word: śrī-kṛṣṇasya anudhyānena — through continuous meditation on Śrī Kṛṣṇa; nivṛttāḥ aśeṣāḥ cakṣuḥ-ādi-vṛttayaḥ yāsām — whose functions of sight and the other senses had entirely ceased; imam lokam deham api na jānanti sma — they no longer perceived this world or even their own bodies; muktāḥ iva — like liberated persons
15.translation: Through continuous meditation on Śrī Kṛṣṇa, all the activities of their senses, beginning with sight, ceased. They no longer perceived this world or even their own bodies, like liberated persons.

16.word_for_word: aparāḥ striyaḥ — other women; śaureḥ giraḥ smarantyaḥ — remembering Śauri's words; saṃmumuhuḥ — became utterly bewildered; anurāgeṇa yat smitam tena īritāḥ — uttered with a smile arising from affection; hṛdi-spṛśaḥ — touching the heart, charming; citrāṇi padāni yāsu — containing striking expressions
16.translation: Other women, remembering Śauri's words, became utterly overwhelmed. Those words had been uttered with smiles born of affection; they touched the heart, were enchanting, and contained striking and varied expressions.

18.word_for_word: viraheṇa kātarāḥ — distressed by separation; vihvalāḥ — overwhelmed; acyute āśayaḥ cittam yāsām — whose minds were fixed in Acyuta
18.translation: They were distressed and overwhelmed by the prospect of separation, their minds wholly fixed upon Acyuta.

19.word_for_word: kṛṣṇa-saṅgatim vidhāya vighaṭṭayati — having arranged union with Kṛṣṇa, the Creator now breaks it apart; vidhātāram pratyekam ākrośantyaḥ — each of them reproaching the Creator; maitryā — by friendly conduct, acts of benefit; praṇayena — by affection; akṛtārthān — not yet fulfilled; aprāpta-bhogān api — who have not yet enjoyed their desired union; tān viyuṅkṣi — you separate them; tasmāt na tava dayā — therefore you have no compassion; bāliśaḥ api tvam — you are childish or foolish; apārthakam — purposeless
19.translation: Each gopī reproaches the Creator who first arranged their meeting with Kṛṣṇa and now breaks it apart: ‘Through friendship and affection you bring beings together, yet before their purpose is fulfilled and before they have enjoyed that union, you separate them. Therefore you have no compassion.’ They even call him foolish: his action is ‘apārthaka,’ without proper purpose.

20.word_for_word: vigarhitaṃ tava idam karma — this act of yours is blameworthy; śokam apanudad iti śoka-apanodaḥ — that which dispels sorrow; smita-leśaḥ — slight smile; gūḍha-hāsaḥ — subtle laughter; tena sundaram mukundasya vaktram — Mukunda's face made beautiful by it; sakṛt pradarśya — having shown it once; punaḥ pārokṣyam adṛśyatām karoṣi — you again make it unseen; asādhu nindyam — wrong and condemnable
20.translation: They say that the Creator's act is blameworthy: ‘You showed us once the face of Mukunda, beautiful with the faint, hidden smile that dispels sorrow, and now you make that very face invisible again. What you have done is wrong and deserving of blame.’

21.word_for_word: datta-apahāritvena ati-krūraḥ tvam — you are exceedingly cruel because you take back what you gave; nanu akrūraḥ harati na aham — objection: Akrūra is taking him, not I; akrūra-samākhyayā — under the name Akrūra; na hi evam kartum anyaḥ prabhavati — no one else has power to do this; nāma-antareṇa tvam eva āgataḥ asi — you yourself have come under another name; tvad-dattena cakṣuṣā — with the eyes given by you; madhudviṣaḥ eka-deśe netra-vaktra-ādau — in portions of Madhudviṣ's form, such as his eyes and face; tvadīyam samagram sṛṣṭi-naipuṇyam adrākṣma — we saw the full perfection of your creative skill; tat cakṣuḥ — those very eyes; asmān andhī-karoṣi — you now make us blind
21.translation: They accuse the Creator of being cruel because he takes back what he himself bestowed. If he objects, ‘Akrūra is taking Kṛṣṇa away, not I,’ they answer: ‘Under the name Akrūra you yourself have surely come, because no one else could have the power to do this. With the eyes you gave us we saw, in Kṛṣṇa's eyes, face and other features, the complete perfection of your creative art; now, as though resentful that your secret skill has been discovered, you separate us from him and make those very eyes blind.’

22.word_for_word: vidhātāram vihāya parasparam ūcuḥ — leaving aside the Creator, they speak among themselves; bata — expression of grief; kṣaṇa-bhaṅgam asthiram sauhṛdam yasya — whose friendship breaks in a moment and is unstable; gṛha-ādīn vihāya — abandoning home and other ties; sākṣāt tasya eva dāsyam upagatāḥ — having entered directly into his service; sva-kṛta-āturāḥ — made distressed by him himself; tat-kṛtena smita-ādinā paravaśāḥ — rendered helpless by his smiles and the like; naḥ na samīkṣate — he does not look upon us; navam navam priyam yasya — one who always finds a new beloved
22.translation: Leaving the Creator aside, the gopīs speak among themselves: ‘Alas, Nanda's son has a friendship that breaks in a moment. We abandoned home and everything else and entered directly into his service; he himself made us heartsick and helpless through his smiles and other charms, yet now he does not even look at us. He is always finding some new beloved.’ Thus they resolve that he must be stopped.

23.word_for_word: sa-īrṣyam ūcuḥ — they speak with jealousy; sukham prabhāta — blessed is the dawn; vraja-spateḥ śrī-kṛṣṇasya mukham pāsyanti — they will drink in, behold eagerly, Śrī Kṛṣṇa's face; apāṅgena — by the corner of the eye; utkalitam smitam eva āsavaḥ rasaḥ yasmin — whose intoxicating nectar is the smile blossoming from his sidelong glance; yad vā — alternatively; apāṅga-utkalita-smitena āsava-rūpam yat mukham — a face itself like intoxicating nectar because of that smile
23.translation: With jealousy they say, ‘How fortunate will be the women of Mathurā at dawn: they will drink in the face of the Lord of Vraja.’ The intoxicating nectar of that face is the smile blossoming from the corners of his eyes. Alternatively, because of the smile rising from his sidelong glance, the entire face itself is compared to intoxicating nectar; hence the verb of ‘drinking’ is especially apt.

24.word_for_word: dvitrāṇi dināni tathā bhavatu — suppose it is so for two or three days; asmat-sneha-ākṛṣṭaḥ — drawn back by our affection; pitrā-ādibhiḥ parāvartitaḥ — turned back by his father and others; āgamiṣyati iti āśaṅkya — thinking perhaps he will return; madhuvat-mañjubhiḥ bhāṣitaiḥ — by their speech sweet as honey; vaśīkṛta-cittaḥ — his mind captivated; salajja-smitaiḥ vibhramaiḥ — by bashful smiles and charms; bhraman paravān — wandering under another's control; vraje pare bandhavaḥ santi yasya — one who has other relatives in Vraja; manasvī dhīraḥ api — though high-minded and steady; grāmyā avidagdhāḥ naḥ katham pratiyāsyate — how will he return to us rustic, unsophisticated women?
24.translation: They consider the hope that perhaps, after two or three days, Kṛṣṇa will be drawn back by their affection or sent back by his father and relatives. Then they reject it: ‘The women there will captivate his mind with speech sweet as honey and with bashful smiles and alluring gestures. Even if he still has other relatives here in Vraja and is naturally steady and high-minded, how could he return to rustic, unsophisticated women like us? He will not.’

25.word_for_word: asmat-utsava-bhājaḥ anye eva adya bhaviṣyanti — today others will possess the festival that was ours; tatra pure dāśārha-ādīnām dṛśaḥ mahān utsavaḥ bhaviṣyati — in that city the sight of the Dāśārhas and others will become a great festival; ye devakī-sutam drakṣyanti — those who see Devakī's son; ye ca adhvani gacchantam drakṣyanti — and those who see him along the road; teṣām api dṛśaḥ — for their eyes too; yad vā dṛśaḥ iti dvitīyā — alternatively dṛśaḥ is accusative; netrāṇi mahotsavam prāpsyanti — their eyes will attain a great festival
25.translation: They say, ‘Today others will become the recipients of the festival that belonged to us. In the city, the eyes of the Dāśārhas and others who see Devakī's son will enjoy a great festival, and so will the eyes of everyone who sees him along the road.’ Alternatively, the grammar can mean that their very eyes will attain that great festival.

26.word_for_word: akrūram śapantyaḥ — cursing Akrūra; etad-vidhasya — one whose action is of this sort; niṣkṛpasya — merciless; akrūra iti śobhanam nāma mā bhūt — let the fine name ‘Akrūra, not cruel’ not belong to him; atīva dāruṇaḥ — exceedingly harsh; priyāt prāṇāt api priyataram kṛṣṇam — Kṛṣṇa, dearer even than life; adhvanaḥ pāram — far along the road; asmat-dṛg-agocaratvāt ati-dūram deśam — a place so distant that he passes beyond the range of our eyes; neṣyati — he will take him
26.translation: They curse Akrūra: ‘For a merciless man who performs an act like this, the beautiful name Akrūra—“not cruel”—is wholly inappropriate. He is exceedingly harsh, for he will take Kṛṣṇa, who is dearer to us even than life, so far along the road that he passes completely beyond the range of our eyes.’

27.word_for_word: aho dhik asmat-jīvitam — alas, shame upon our lives; anārdra-dhīḥ — hard-hearted; eṣa kṛṣṇaḥ ratham adhirūḍhaḥ — this Kṛṣṇa has mounted the chariot; asya avinayam ālakṣya sthaviraiḥ upekṣitam — the elders see this impropriety yet ignore it; te na nivāritavantaḥ — they have not stopped it; daivam — fate; yadi daivam anukūlam bhavet — if fate were favorable to us; vighnaiḥ kaścit pratihanyeta — some obstacle would stop them; vajra-pātaḥ vā — or a sudden lightning strike; anyat aniṣṭam vā — or some other mishap; na tat kiñcit asti — but nothing of the kind occurs
27.translation: ‘Alas, shame upon our lives!’ They call Kṛṣṇa hard-hearted because he has actually mounted the chariot; the elders see the impropriety of taking him away yet do nothing to stop it. Nor is fate on their side. If fate favored them, some obstacle would surely intervene—a sudden thunderbolt or some other mishap—but nothing at all occurs.

28.word_for_word: parasparam saṃmantrya — consulting together; sāhasam adhiruhya — resolving upon a bold act; nivārayāma iti — ‘let us stop him’; akariṣyan kariṣyanti — future sense: they will do it; nimiṣa-ardha-dustyajān — impossible to leave even for half a blink; mukunda-saṅgāt vidhvaṃsitāni viyojitāni — torn away from Mukunda's company; dīnāni cetāṃsi yāsām — whose hearts are therefore wretched; na mṛtyoḥ api bhayam — they do not fear even death
28.translation: After consulting one another, the gopīs resolve on a daring course: ‘Let us stop him.’ The verbal form has future force: they are about to act. Their hearts, unable to bear separation from Mukunda even for half the blink of an eye, have now been torn from his company and made utterly desolate; in such a state they no longer fear even death.

29.word_for_word: avaśyam sāhasam eva avalambanīyam — we must certainly resort to this bold act; lalitam smitam — graceful smile; valgu mantraḥ — charming conversation; līlā-avalokaḥ — playful glance; parirambhaṇam — embrace; anurāgeṇa — with love; rāsa-goṣṭhyām — in the assembly of the rāsa dance; kṣaṇadāḥ rātrayaḥ kṣaṇam iva nītāḥ — nights passed like a single moment; tam kṛṣṇam vinā — without that Kṛṣṇa; durantam tamaḥ viraha-duḥkham — endless darkness, the sorrow of separation; katham atitarem — how could we cross it?; na kathañcit — in no way
29.translation: They give another reason why they must resort to a bold attempt. In the rāsa assembly, through Kṛṣṇa's graceful smile, charming words, playful glances and embraces filled with love, whole nights passed for them like a single moment. ‘Without that Kṛṣṇa, how could we ever cross the endless darkness of separation? We could not.’

30.word_for_word: āstām tamaḥ-atitaraṇam — leave aside the question of crossing that darkness; jīvanam eva katham syāt — how could life itself continue?; ahnaḥ kṣaye — at day's end; khura-rajobhiḥ churitāḥ dhūsarāḥ alakāḥ srajaḥ ca yasya — whose locks and garland were grayed by dust from the cows' hooves; vrajam viśan — entering Vraja; smitena yat kaṭākṣa-nirīkṣaṇam — the sidelong glance accompanied by a smile; naḥ cittam kṣiṇoti harati — steals our minds; amum kṛṣṇam vinā katham bhavema jīvema — without that Kṛṣṇa, how could we live?
30.translation: ‘Never mind crossing the darkness of separation—how could we even remain alive?’ At the close of day Kṛṣṇa would enter Vraja with his curls and garland made gray by the dust of the cows' hooves, and with a smiling sidelong glance he would steal their minds. ‘Without that Kṛṣṇa, how can we possibly continue to live?’

31.word_for_word: kṛṣṇe viṣaktāni mānasāni yāsām — whose minds were wholly attached to Kṛṣṇa; su-svaram uccaiḥ — loudly in sweet voices; krūram akrūrataḥ śrutvā kaṃsam — hearing from Akrūra of cruel Kaṃsa; kaṃsa-niṣūdanaḥ — the destroyer of Kaṃsa; gopī-manoratha-ārāmaḥ — the delight of the gopīs' desires; sa-rāmaḥ sva-puram yayau — together with Rāma he went toward his own city
31.translation: Their minds were completely fastened upon Kṛṣṇa, and they cried out loudly in sweet voices. Having heard from Akrūra about the cruelty of Kaṃsa, Kṛṣṇa—the future destroyer of Kaṃsa and the delight in whom the gopīs' desires rested—set out for his own city together with Rāma.

32.word_for_word: tāḥ anādṛtya — not responding to those women; kṛta-maitra-ādikaḥ — having performed the rite beginning with maitra; maitram mitra-daivatam sandhyopāsanam — the evening worship whose deity is Mitra; tad-ādi-karma kṛtam yena — who performed that and the other prescribed rites
32.translation: Without responding directly to the women's cries, Akrūra performed his prescribed evening observances. ‘Maitra’ refers to the sandhyā worship connected with the deity Mitra and the other rites accompanying it.

33.word_for_word: anvasajjanta — they followed after; anvagacchan — they went behind the chariot
33.translation: ‘Anvasajjanta’ means that the gopīs followed behind the departing chariot.

34.word_for_word: anurañjitāḥ — somewhat comforted and gladdened; parāvṛtya nirīkṣaṇa-ādibhiḥ — by Kṛṣṇa turning back to look at them and similar gestures; pratyādeśam — dismissal; pratyākhyānam — being sent back
34.translation: Kṛṣṇa's turning back to look at them and similar gestures gave them a little comfort. ‘Pratyādeśa’ means that he directed them to return, sending them back.

35.word_for_word: tapyatīḥ — burning with pain; santapyamānāḥ — deeply afflicted; āyāsye — ‘I shall come’; śīghram āgamiṣyāmi — ‘I shall return soon’; dūta-vākyaiḥ — by messages sent through a messenger
35.translation: As they burned in grief, they were sustained by messages sent back to them: ‘I shall come; I shall return soon.’

36.word_for_word: kṛṣṇam anu prasthāpitāḥ ātmānaḥ cittāni yābhiḥ — whose very selves, their minds, had been sent away following Kṛṣṇa; lekhya-maya-putrikāḥ iva — like painted figures; niścalāḥ — motionless
36.translation: Their very selves—their minds—had departed after Kṛṣṇa. They therefore remained motionless, like figures painted upon a picture.

39.word_for_word: vṛkṣāṇām ṣaṇḍam samūham — a grove, a group of trees; upavrajya — approaching it
39.translation: ‘Ṣaṇḍa’ means a grove or cluster of trees; they approached such a grove.

40.word_for_word: śatrubhyaḥ śaṅkitaḥ san — being wary of enemies; ratha-upari niveśya — seating them on the chariot
40.translation: Akrūra, remaining wary of possible enemies, had the two brothers stay seated upon the chariot.

41.word_for_word: brahma vedam japan — reciting Vedic mantra; eva-śabdaḥ pratibimba-vyāvṛtti-arthaḥ — the word eva excludes the possibility of a mere reflection; kva imau bālau kva tau mallau — ‘where are these two boys, and where are those mighty wrestlers?’; śaṅkita-cetase akrūrāya — to Akrūra, whose mind was anxious; jale rūpam atyāścaryam vyadarśayat — he showed an exceedingly wondrous form in the water
41.translation: Akrūra entered the water reciting Vedic mantra. The particle ‘eva’ is used to exclude the idea that what he saw was merely a reflection. Because Akrūra had been anxious—‘How can these two young boys possibly face those enormous wrestlers?’—the Lord revealed to him in the water an astonishing divine form.

44.word_for_word: siddha-ādibhiḥ — by the Siddhas and others; stūyamānam — being praised
44.translation: He saw the Lord being praised by the Siddhas and other celestial beings.

45.word_for_word: sahasram śirāṃsi yasya — having a thousand heads; sahasra-phaṇeṣu maulayaḥ yasya — having crowns upon his thousand hoods; nīle ambare yasya — wearing blue garments; bisa-vat kamala-nāla-vat śvetam — white like a lotus stalk; śṛṅgaiḥ śikharaiḥ śvetam kailāsam iva — like white Mount Kailāsa with its peaks
45.translation: The serpent form had a thousand heads and crowns upon its thousand hoods and wore blue garments. His body was white like the stalk of a lotus, standing like snow-white Mount Kailāsa with its many peaks.

46.word_for_word: tasya utsaṅge — upon his lap; kuṇḍalī-kṛta-deha-ardhe — upon the half of his body arranged in coils; vilokya — seeing; ekādaśena ślokena anvayaḥ — the construction continues through eleven verses
46.translation: The Lord was seen upon the lap formed by the coiled portion of that serpent's body. The grammatical construction beginning with ‘seeing’ continues through the following eleven verses.

47.word_for_word: śobhane bhruvau yasya — having beautiful eyebrows; unnatā nāsikā yasya — having a prominent nose; śobhanau kapolau yasya — having beautiful cheeks; aruṇau adharau yasya — having reddish lips
47.translation: His eyebrows were beautiful, his nose prominent and graceful, his cheeks lovely, and his lips reddish.

48.word_for_word: tuṅgau aṃsau yasya — whose shoulders were high; uraḥ-sthale śrīḥ yasya — whose chest bore Śrī; valimat — marked by transverse folds; pallava-udaram — belly like a tender leaf; aśvattha-dala-sadṛśam — resembling a peepal leaf
48.translation: His shoulders were high and his chest bore Śrī. His abdomen showed graceful transverse folds and was shaped like a tender leaf, specifically like the leaf of an aśvattha tree.

49.word_for_word: kaṭi-taṭam ca śroṇiḥ ca — waist and hips; karabha-sadṛśam ūru-dvayam — pair of thighs resembling an elephant's trunk; bṛhat — broad; anvitam — endowed with
49.translation: He had a broad waist and hips and a pair of powerful thighs compared to the trunk of a young elephant. The compound may be construed either as one broad complex of waist, hips and thighs, or as broad waist and hips together with the elephant-like thighs.

50.word_for_word: tuṅgau īṣat unnatau gulphau — ankles slightly raised and shapely; aruṇa-nakha-vrātāḥ — clusters of reddish nails; teṣām dīdhitibhiḥ — by their rays; navāḥ komalāḥ aṅgulyaḥ aṅguṣṭhau ca — fresh tender toes and great toes; tāni eva dalāni — those themselves like petals; vilasat pāda-paṅkajam — shining lotus feet
50.translation: His ankles were shapely and slightly raised. The reddish nails radiated light; his fresh, tender toes and great toes formed, as it were, the petals of his splendid lotus feet.

51-52.word_for_word: su-mahārhāḥ maṇi-vrātāḥ yeṣu — containing collections of exceedingly precious jewels; kirīṭa-ādibhiḥ — by crown and the other ornaments
51-52.translation: His crown and other ornaments were set with clusters of exceedingly precious jewels.

53.word_for_word: pṛthak pṛthak bhāvaḥ abhiprāyaḥ yeṣām — each group having a distinct conception or intention; pārṣadaiḥ svāmī iti — by the attendants as ‘our Lord’; sanaka-ādibhiḥ brahma iti — by Sanaka and others as Brahman; brahma-ādyaiḥ maheśvara iti — by Brahmā and others as the Supreme Lord; marīci-ādibhiḥ dvija-uttamaiḥ paraḥ prajāpatiḥ iti — by Marīci and other foremost brāhmaṇas as the supreme progenitor; vasuḥ uparicaraḥ — Uparicara Vasu; prahlāda-nārada-vasavaḥ pramukhāḥ — headed by Prahlāda, Nārada and the Vasus; param daivatam iti — as the supreme deity; śreṣṭhaiḥ vacobhiḥ — with excellent words
53.translation: The various groups praised him according to their distinct conceptions. His attendants praised him as their Master; Sanaka and the other sages as Brahman; Brahmā and the gods as the Supreme Lord; Marīci and the foremost brāhmaṇas as the supreme Prajāpati. Uparicara Vasu is also included. Groups headed by Prahlāda, Nārada and the Vasus praised him as the supreme Deity, each with fitting and excellent words.

55.word_for_word: vidyā-avidye — knowledge and ignorance; jīvānām mukti-saṃsṛti-hetū — causes respectively of liberation and transmigration for living beings; māyā tayoḥ kāraṇam — māyā is the underlying cause of both; śaktiḥ — potency; hlādinī — bliss potency; saṃvit-jñānam — consciousness/knowledge potency; ābhiḥ anyābhiḥ ca niṣevitam — served by these and other powers
55.translation: Vidyā and avidyā are respectively causes of liberation and transmigration for living beings, while māyā is their underlying source. The Lord is also attended by his potencies such as hlādinī, the power of bliss, and saṃvit, the power of conscious knowledge, together with other powers.

56.word_for_word: vilokya su-bhṛśam prītaḥ — seeing this, intensely delighted; asmat-kṛṣṇaḥ asau evaṃ-bhūtaḥ parameśvaraḥ iti jñātvā — realizing ‘this very Kṛṣṇa of ours is such a Supreme Lord’
56.translation: Seeing all this, Akrūra was filled with extraordinary joy, realizing: ‘This very Kṛṣṇa who is ours is none other than the Supreme Lord of this exalted nature.’
